question: After the trilogue negotiations, the following text was agreed in Annex 10 to a new Packaging Regulation: ‘Member States with regions with high transboundary business shall ensure that the deposit and return systems allows for collection of packaging from other Member States’ deposit and return systems at designated collection points and shall endeavour to enable the possibility of return of a deposit that was charged to the end user when purchasing the packaging.

’ Can an operator in a border area of a Member State who sells to consumers residing in another Member State on the other side of the border opt not to charge a deposit on purchases by end consumers on the ground that the Member State in which the consumer resides does not meet the requirements of the above text?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (10.7.2024) Annex X of the provisionally agreed Packaging and Packaging Waste Regulation1 lays down minimum requirements for deposit and return systems (DRS).

To ensure the smooth operation of DRS in border regions with high transboundary business, the legislators have agreed to require Member States to allow for the collection of packaging from other Member States’ DRS at designated collection points and endeavour to enable the return of deposits charged to the end user when purchasing the packaging.

Article 50(9) of the provisionally agreed regulation provides for the application of the requirements of Annex X as of 1 January 2029. Member States with existing DRS that achieve 90% separate collection of the targeted packaging formats by 1 January 2029 are exempted from those requirements but should nonetheless endeavour to ensure compliance with them when reviewing DRS.
Member States with existing DRS that do not meet that target are required to apply Annex X as of 2035. The text quoted in the question is in Annex X of the provisionally agreed Regulation.

However, Article 50(2) requires Member States to ensure that DRS are set up for single use plastic bottles and cans for beverages and that a deposit is charged at the point of sale and does not provide for exemptions from this requirement that would be linked to the residence of consumers in other Member States.

Article 50(3) allows Member States to derogate from the obligation laid down in Article 50(2) subject to conditions linked to high levels of separate collection of the targeted packaging formats. Allowing the practice of not charging a deposit as described in the question could be considered on a case-by-case basis where the conditions laid down in the Regulation for derogating from Article 50(2) are met.
